statement.p: (b) Find the best linear approximation of g(x,y) for (x,y) near (4,2).
(c) Use the approximation in part (b) to estimate g(4.03, 1.97).

static.solution:
(a) We have g_x = \frac{x}{\sqrt{x^{2}+3y+14}}, \quad \hbox{ so } g_x(4, 2) = \frac{2}{3} and g_y = \frac{3}{2 \sqrt{x^{2}+3y+14}}, \quad \hbox{ so } g_y(4, 2) = \frac{1}{4}. Thus \nabla g(4,2) = \frac{2}{3}\, \vec i + \frac{1}{4}\, \vec j.
(b) Using the value g(4, 2) = 6 and the partial derivatives in part (a) we have g(x, y) = \sqrt{x^{2}+3y+14} \approx 6 + \frac{2}{3} (x-4) + \frac{1}{4} (y-2).
(c) Using the linearization in part (b), we have g(4.03, 1.97) \approx 6 + \frac{2}{3} (4 - 4.03) + \frac{1}{4} (2 - 1.97) = 6.0125.
